_meta.title: Varṇa word-formation lexicon — binding (in-combination) reading (consonants + vowels)
_meta.governing_axis: The reading axis is BIND vs LIBERATE, which is ORTHOGONAL to good vs bad. Binding = contractive / holding / attachment-forming (fixes or limits consciousness). Liberating = expansive / unbinding / releasing. This is a state of expression, NOT a moral judgement: dharma is BINDING (it holds you to your stance, dhṛ = to hold) even though it is 'good'; adharma is LIBERATING (it breaks the stance, unbinds) even though it is 'bad'; hope (āśā) is binding (forward-grasping), cruelty is binding (contractive), mokṣa is liberating (releasing).
_meta.word_formation_rule: A varṇa is sattvic / unbound in ISOLATION and BINDS when it enters COMBINATION (a word), because manifestation is contraction into form. Therefore `word_formation_reading` = the BINDING (in-combination, contractive) pole of every varṇa, and is the field to use when reading a word. The liberating pole is the at-rest / isolated / completed state (recoverable: it is the `counter_pole` for the 28 affliction-rooted consonants and for kṣa, and the `worldly_vritti` / Sarkar root for ca, ra, sa, ha; for va it is `counter_pole` = Adharma).
_meta.purpose: Primary field `word_formation_reading` gives the binding/in-combination expression used in word formation. `worldly_vritti` (Sarkar's source root) and `counter_pole` are retained for provenance.
_meta.source: P.R. Sarkar (Shrii Shrii Anandamurti), 'Acoustic Roots of the Indo-Aryan Alphabet' (1984-85, Calcutta), verified line-by-line against the source.
word_formation_flip_changelog: ca: word_formation_reading = Aviveka (binding). Sarkar's root viveka is the liberating/at-rest pole. (binding gloss derived.)
ra: word_formation_reading = Sarvanāśa (binding). SOURCE-FAITHFUL — Sarkar gives ra both vitality (liberating) and sarvanāśa (binding).

va: word_formation_reading = Dharma (binding) — dharma HOLDS/sustains the stance, so it binds on the non-moral axis; Adharma is the liberating (unbinding) pole. Sarkar's root retained as worldly_vritti.
sa: word_formation_reading = escapism (binding); Sarkar's root mokṣa/sattva is the liberating pole. (binding gloss derived.)

ha: word_formation_reading = Rātri / night (binding) — corrected to RĀTRI (night/darkness, the contractive opposite of ha=day/sun/light), dropping the abstract 'avidyā'; parā-vidyā is the liberating pole. (binding gloss derived.)

kṣa: word_formation_reading = Aparā-vidyā (mundane knowledge) — LEFT as mundane knowledge (worldly/binding), NOT flipped; liberating pole = Parā-vidyā (spiritual knowledge). (Reverted earlier mithyā-jñāna flip.)
The other 28 consonants (and kṣa): word_formation_reading = worldly_vritti (already the worldly/binding root).
_meta._status: FAITHFUL DOCTRINAL TRANSCRIPTION + a stated binding-in-combination reading convention. NOT empirically validated: the pre-registered blind signal tests on this lexicon returned NO_SIGNAL (real ≈ scrambled). For word-formation reading / contemplative authoring, not a validated sound→meaning decoder.
_meta.scope: consonants (33 + kṣa): SOURCE-GROUNDED (P.R. Sarkar, verified). vowels (12): CANDIDATE / INTUITION-DERIVED — vowels are NOT vṛtti roots in the source (they are roots of musical notes, creation/preservation/destruction, and cosmological/vocalization functions); their vṛtti-style glosses are interpretive. Both sections use the binding-in-combination reading; the vowel section remains EXPLORATORY (see PREREG_OBJECT_PROFILE_FIT.md §16).
_meta.polarity_values: polarity describes SARKAR'S ROOT on a sustaining/binding/mundane sense and is retained for provenance only; word_formation_reading is ALWAYS the binding pole regardless of polarity.
_meta.fields: iast, deva, varga, worldly_vritti (Sarkar root), polarity (Sarkar-root descriptor), element (where stated), word_formation_reading (binding/in-combination — USE THIS), counter_pole{sanskrit,english,type,derived}, source_quote
_meta.reading_order: RULES ARE APPLIED BEFORE MEANING. 1) romanization identifies the varṇa (IAST canonical; popular_roman is the English spelling); 2) the bind/liberate axis (non-moral) selects the pole; 3) word_formation_reading (the binding pole) gives the meaning. Spelling never changes which varṇa or which meaning.
_meta._romanization_rule: IAST (`iast`) is CANONICAL for interop (Monier-Williams, g2p) and is kept unchanged. `popular_roman` is the English-facing display per the user's convention: palatal च='cha', छ='chha'; retroflex aspirates ठ='thha', ढ='dhha'; retroflex sibilant ष='shha'; unaspirated retroflex stops ट='tta', ड='dda'. popular_roman is spelling only — it never changes the varṇa identity or its meaning.
_meta._vowel_provenance: Vowel word_formation_reading = the binding/distortion pole of the vowel's active essence; the active essence (birth, expansion, completion, …) is the liberating/at-rest pole. These glosses are intuition-derived, not source-grounded like the consonants, and must not be treated as evidence.

ka.element: flowing water (ka = water; 'that which produces sound')
ka.source_quote: Ka is the acoustic root of the abhīpsātmaka āśā vṛtti. It is also the acoustic root of Kārya Brahma.

kha.source_quote: The acoustic root of cintā vṛtti [worry] is kha. Impersonal thoughts are symbolized by kha.

worldly_vritti.english: effort / striving to arouse dormant potential

ga.source_quote: The effort made to arouse one's dormant potentiality is called ceṣṭā. Ga is the acoustic root of ceṣṭā vṛtti.

worldly_vritti.english: attachment / love bound by time, space, individuality

gha.source_quote: Mamatā, the vṛtti of love and attachment, is related to time, space and individuality. Gha is the acoustic root of mamatā vṛtti.

nga.source_quote: Uṋa is the acoustic root of dambha vṛtti [the propensity of vanity].

ca.source_quote: Ca is the acoustic root of viveka [conscience].
ca._note: Sarkar's root viveka is the LIBERATING (at-rest) pole; the binding/in-combination reading is its absence, aviveka (derived). Cf. your example: while the ca is in combination it expresses aviveka; viveka is reached at completion.

worldly_vritti.english: nervous breakdown / collapse of a functioning mind

cha.source_quote: Cha is the acoustic root of vikalatā vṛtti [nervous breakdown].

ja.source_quote: Ja is the acoustic root of ahaṁkāra vṛtti (ego). The ego becomes inflated when one allows one's 'I' feeling to take a predominant role.

jha.source_quote: Jha is the acoustic root of lolupatā, lobha [greed] and lolatā [avarice] vṛttis.

nya.source_quote: Iṋa is the acoustic root of kapaṭatā vṛtti [hypocrisy].

tta.source_quote: Ṭa is the acoustic root of vitarka vṛtti [overstating one's case]. Vitarka is a combination of a bad temper and garrulousness.

ttha.source_quote: Ṭha is the acoustic root of anutāpa vṛtti [repentance].

dda.source_quote: Ḍa is the acoustic root of lajjā vṛtti [the propensity of shyness].

ddha.source_quote: Senseless, sadistic killing is called piśunatā vṛtti. [Ḍha is its acoustic root.]

nna.source_quote: Ṇa is the acoustic root of īrṣā vṛtti [the propensity of envy].

worldly_vritti.english: staticity, deep sleep, intellectual dullness, spiritual inertia

ta.source_quote: Ta is the acoustic root of staticity, long sleep and deep sleep, and of intellectual dullness and spiritual inertness.

tha.source_quote: Tha is the acoustic root of viṣāda vṛtti, of melancholy.

da.source_quote: Da is the acoustic root of peevishness.

worldly_vritti.english: thirst for acquisition (wealth, name, fame, power, prestige)

dha.source_quote: Dha is the acoustic root of thirst for acquisition. This limitless craving is called tṛṣṇā in Sanskrit.

worldly_vritti.english: blind attachment / infatuation (deśa, kāla, idea, ādhāra)

na.source_quote: Na is the acoustic root of moha vṛtti [blind attachment or infatuation].

pa.source_quote: Pa is the acoustic root of ghṛṇā vṛtti [hatred or revulsion]. Pa is the acoustic root of the fetter of hatred.

pha.source_quote: Pha is the acoustic root of bhaya vṛtti [the propensity of fear].

ba.source_quote: Ba is the acoustic root of avajñā vṛtti [indifference].

worldly_vritti.english: deluded obsession (loss of common sense under a ripu's spell)

bha.source_quote: Bha is the acoustic root of the mūrcchā vṛtti. It means to lose one's common sense under the hypnotic spell of a particular ripu.

worldly_vritti.english: annihilation; and giving latitude / indulgence (Hindi baṛhvā denā)

ma.source_quote: Ma is the acoustic root of praṇāśa [annihilation]. It is also the acoustic root of praśraya vṛtti – giving latitude [indulgence].

worldly_vritti.english: lack of confidence (in self and others); also constant movement

ya.element: constant movement (like the movement of air)
ya.source_quote: Ya is the acoustic root of aviśvāsa vṛtti [lack of confidence], and is also the acoustic root of constant movement (like the movement of air).

word_formation_reading.english: defeatist annihilation-thought ('everything is gone, I am undone')

ra.source_quote: Ra is the acoustic root of agnitattva or prāṇaśakti – vitality. It is also the acoustic root of sarvanāśa [the thought of annihilation]. The monosyllabic word ra means 'fire'.
ra._note: SOURCE-FAITHFUL flip: Sarkar gives ra both poles. The binding/in-combination reading is sarvanāśa (contractive collapse); the liberating/at-rest pole is vitality/fire.

la.source_quote: La is the acoustic root of krūratā vṛtti [cruelty]. La is also the acoustic root of kṣititattva, the solid factor.

worldly_vritti.english: ensconcement in one's original stance; the sustaining principle

word_formation_reading.english: holding / ensconcement in original stance (BINDS — dhṛ = to hold; non-moral)

counter_pole.english: non-conforming / deviation from stance (UNBINDS → liberating / at-rest pole)

va.source_quote: Va is the acoustic root of dharma. Va is also the acoustic root of jalatattva [the liquid factor], and of the rain-god Varuṇa Deva.
va._note: SPECIAL on the non-moral bind/release axis: dharma HOLDS/sustains the stance → it is the BINDING (in-combination) reading, even though it is 'good'. Adharma is non-conforming → it UNBINDS → it is the liberating / at-rest pole, even though it is 'bad'. 'Liberating' here means unbinding, not endorsement.

worldly_vritti.english: the mutative principle; psychic longing / material pursuit (artha)

counter_pole.english: transmutation of dynamism into purposeful accomplishment

sha.source_quote: Śa is the acoustic root of rajoguṇa [the mutative principle]. It is also the acoustic root of artha [psychic longing].

worldly_vritti.english: the static principle; all physical / worldly desires (kāma)

ssa.source_quote: Ṣa is the acoustic root of tamoguṇa [the static principle], and of all kinds of worldly desires … kāma.

sa.source_quote: Sa is the acoustic root of mokṣa [unqualified liberation]. Sa is the acoustic root of sattvaguṇa [the sentient principle].
sa._note: Sarkar's root mokṣa/sattva is the LIBERATING (at-rest) pole; the binding/in-combination reading is its worldly distortion, escapism / static withdrawal (derived).

worldly_vritti.english: intuitional science; ethereal factor, daytime, the sun, svarloka

word_formation_reading.english: night / darkness (the contractive opposite of ha = day / sun / light)

counter_pole.english: intuitional knowledge / day / sun (liberating / at-rest pole)

ha.source_quote: Ha is the acoustic root of the ethereal factor, of daytime, of the sun, of svarloka, and of parā-vidyā [intuitional science].
ha._note: Binding reading corrected to RĀTRI (night/darkness, the contractive pole), dropping the abstract 'avidyā'. Sarkar's root (day/sun/parā-vidyā) is the liberating/at-rest pole; ha's stated opposite ṭha = night/moon supports rātri as the dark pole.

ksha.source_quote: Kṣa is the acoustic root of mundane knowledge, and is also the acoustic root of material science.
ksha._note: Mundane knowledge (aparā-vidyā) IS the worldly/binding reading; its liberating opposite is spiritual knowledge (parā-vidyā) — the classical parā/aparā-vidyā pairing. Earlier mithyā-jñāna flip reverted.
